package: B1 P1: the slot version 2 codec, the stable prefix reader and the readers in every format; B1 P2a: the lifecycle store transitions, the suspend, lift, markRetiring and markRetired transactions, the publication refusal and the writer rules; B1 P2b checkpoint 1: the boot facts, the deletion or migration step, confirm disposal and Restore; B1 P2c: Restore's claim and phase fixes and the gated release engine at the persistence level, with its capability, its store primitives and the source rules that keep release unreachable; B1 P3: Settings seeding, boot facts, the retired boot rule and the release finish; B1 P4: the manager's lifecycle operations beside the old ones, their format refusals before any effect, the suspension closure, every activation point's suspension refusal, the gated release with the retired boot rule, and the source rules that keep every new operation without a production caller. B1 P5 checkpoint 1: the pinned inputs of the rollback models of 24bfb6a and 78456b3, and the lifecycle layout emitter with its coverage check. B1 P5 checkpoint 2: the rollback models of 24bfb6a and 78456b3 over every lifecycle layout, B1's readers under Format.V2 and Format.V3, a layout of RELEASING without a directory under a version 2 header, and their controls.
basis: Each count is the length of the runner's case lists. Each mutant's catches are traced against the cases it breaks; a defect that another rule also refuses names only the cases that reach it.

round_2.changes: The HOLDS golden orders its two grant entries by actor serial against their grant order, and a new codec case orders entries by class, then actor serial, then grant, refusing each swapped neighbour pair. The reason registry becomes USER_PAUSED 1, CREDENTIAL_EXPOSED 2, SUSPECTED_COMPROMISE 3, RESOURCE_OVERUSE 4, DEVICE_HANDOVER 5, DATA_TRANSFER 6 and RECOVERY_REVIEW 7, each with the actor classes that may use it. The read test pins the older copies' history beside a newer seed.
round_2.not_added: A mutant that drops the actor serial from the order is the same defect as comparing the grant first: two entries of one class always differ in their grant references, so the same cases catch it and no case can tell them apart.

p2a.changes: The store gains the named lifecycle transitions addSuspension, liftSuspension, markSlotRetiring and markSlotRetired with their writer rules, and under Format.V3 its generic update keeps every lifecycle and drops no user. The persistence gains suspend, lift, markRetiring with a Retirement and markRetired, each refused under Format.V1 and V2 before any effect; the version 1 marker and release refuse under Format.V3; publish refuses a suspended binding itself. The read test's Format.V3 marker writer becomes the retire transition, its case names and count unchanged.
p2a.equivalent: The lifecycle format checks at the start of suspend, markRetiring and markRetired: under a slot ceiling of 1 every value they could write is version 2, and the shared slot writer refuses it at the ceiling before any effect, so removing one call leaves no observable difference. The lift check is observable, as an absent entry would be confirmed through a write, and so is the shared predicate.
p2a.development_correction: One prediction was corrected after a development run outside the guard, before any guarded run: publication-check-in-confirmation no longer names the publication case. With the refusal moved into the shared confirmation, the CREATING to LIVE header transition calls that confirmation and refuses before its write, so publication still has no effect. The defect shows where the plan places the refusal: a header phase change of a suspended body, and the confirmations of a repeated suspension and of a durable lift beside another entry, refuse.

p2a_round_2.changes: Under Format.V3 the generic update also keeps every user's serial, with its first case and mutant, and a tombstone's release ticket. Writers allot a version 2 record's six entries one to the account's user, one to a recovery hold and four to grants, so a fifth grant is FULL while the account's user keeps its place; the decoder still accepts any six entries, one per actor. A repeated suspension by the same actor confirms its entry unchanged through the checked writers: SUSPENDED when the request equals it, HELD_UNCHANGED when it differs. The store suite now catches update-past-slot-ceiling too.

p2a_round_2.fault_cases: The repeated suspension sweep now asks with another reason and expects HELD_UNCHANGED. Its names and count stay.
p2a_round_2.equivalent: The user ID half of the V3 identity rule: the generic update's user addition check also refuses a principal moved to another Android user, so only the serial half has a mutant.

p2b_checkpoint_1.changes: NativeIdentityPersistence gains BootFacts and its pure helper bootFacts, built from one durable read: the accounts RETIRED there, the selected ticketed tombstones and the RELEASING entries whose slot reads as missing. The store gains beginSlotDisposition, dischargeSlotDisposition and restoreSlot, the recovery route's writer and the only writer of a recovery hold, with writableDispositionReceipts and writableRecoveryHold. The persistence gains beginDisposition and confirmDisposition, each only in a retired boot, and restore. Each refuses under Format.V1 and V2 before any effect. The existing V1 and V2 store and transaction cases also run the new transitions and transactions, with their names and counts unchanged.
p2b_checkpoint_1.equivalent_checks_without_a_mutant: The lifecycle format checks of beginDisposition and confirmDisposition are equivalent: under Format.V1 and V2 a RETIRED record is a version 2 slot, an unsupported footprint there, so no binding exists for them to reach. The restore mutant removes all three of its format checks together, because each alone is equivalent to the others. The known inventory checks of the two disposition rules are equivalent to the decoder rule that refuses RETIRED with an unknown inventory.

p2c.changes: Restore gets its own claim check, the store's rule for a reservation: another app ID's decoded slot copy, tombstones and their tickets included, or its CREATING entry in any decoded header copy, by package or principal ID. Restore refuses beside any decoded header copy that lists the app ID RELEASING. The persistence gains ReleaseCapability, which carries the key namespace hook, and release, the gated release engine, with ticketUid. The store gains the named release primitives dropReleasedUser, markSlotReleasing and omitReleasedSlot and the rule releasable; under Format.V3 the generic header write turns no entry RELEASING and omits none, and LIVE becomes RELEASING only over a ticketed tombstone. Source rules refuse the capability's construction in production texts and outside its named tests, and every call or method reference of a release entry point outside the release bodies of the persistence. A tombstone's release ticket names a principal ID as sibling evidence, in a valid tombstone and in an unsupported record's decoded copy, as a claim on a reservation, and for the counter bound; a stable prefix need not feed that bound, because only an unsupported record has one. Release checks every remaining copy, and during a continuation the counter and the sibling check are its only guards, each with a case and a mutant. The boot facts give no fact beside an unreadable header copy. restore-under-releasing removes both refusals of RELEASING, because the copy loop covers the selected entry; restore-beside-a-releasing-copy removes the loop alone.
p2c.anchor_updated: restore-beside-a-claim now removes the claimedElsewhere check, Restore's own.
p2c.equivalent_checks_without_a_mutant: The persistence's lifecycle format check of release is equivalent to the store's: under Format.V1 and V2 a RETIRED record and a ticketed tombstone are version 2 slots, unsupported footprints there, so no binding or tombstone exists for it to reach; the mutant release-primitives-under-earlier-formats removes the store primitives' own checks, which a version 1 tombstone reaches. The drop primitive's header phase check is equivalent to the existing refusal of a user drop beside any CREATING header copy. Restore's check of the selected entry's RELEASING phase is covered by its loop over every decoded header copy, which includes the selected one, so no mutant removes it alone. At the start, release's counter and sibling checks are equivalent to the binding's own: a binding above the counter or beside a live sibling is a conflict, never usable; their mutants are caught by continuation cases.
p2c.part_4_living_counts: Unchanged in the binding, history, counter and lab runners and in the lifecycle reads and codec: no case or layout of theirs holds a release ticket, so no load of theirs reads one.

p3.changes: Settings records the boot facts once, from its boot read, after seeding, and defers the package of each RETIRED account, ticketed tombstone and mapped RELEASING entry without a directory. Seeding defers a mapped history that is retiring, retired or suspended. The host facade carries every Settings fragment and restores, observes, seeds and records the boot facts in that order. A source rule refuses bootFacts outside the boot facts fragment, and the primitives rule refuses a method reference of either store writer.

p3_checkpoint_2.changes: The release finish keeps the app ID in the held set and forgets the remembered history until a new Settings instance. The observation and the release finish become fragments that the facade carries verbatim. A new Settings suite runs the seeding, boot facts, retired boot and release body rules through the facade and the history harness. Fragment mutants change the facade and the harness alike, and the two existing Settings mutants move to them. The release rule gains Settings' release finish and the old release path, each allowed only in the manager body that calls it today, until P6.

p4_checkpoint_1.changes: The manager gains its lifecycle operations beside the old ones: suspend, lift, beginRetirement with a retirement block, confirmRetired, beginDisposition, confirmDisposition and releaseUid, with Handle.released. Each refuses under a format without lifecycle records before any effect, including the closure and the pin change. Suspension closes admission in memory first, through Settings' deferral and a mark on the handle, and keeps it through a refused or uncertain write. Preparation, commit, currentIdentity and the published binding check refuse a suspended account. The pins gain finishRelease. The release rule gains releaseUid and finishRelease, and only the manager's gated release calls the engine, Settings' release finish and finishRelease.

p4_checkpoint_2.changes: The manager's gated release is qualified end to end: the retired boot rule for disposition and release, the release body from RETIRED through the durable omission with the app ID held until a new instance, a lost reply acknowledged by a retry in the same instance and freed at the next boot, and its refusals before any effect without a durable releasable RETIRED record, a capability, recorded boot facts or with a suspension closed in memory. A new source rule refuses any production call or method reference of the manager's other lifecycle operations, and of the persistence transactions of the same operations, outside the manager body of that operation.

p4_final.changes: The manager suite's store copy checks the PMS facade's lock at every store load, so a read under the PMS lock fails a case as a directory sync already did; two manager mutants move a read under the lock. The lifecycle rule also covers markRetiring, allowed only in the manager's retirement body, and no longer reads an assert statement as a declaration. The pins' old finish and finishRelease share one copy of the index, so the index copy count stays 2, and the controlled fault test sweeps finishRelease at each index change as it sweeps finishRetire.
